Privacy-first on-device OCR for the Mon language (mnw), spoken by ~1 million people across Myanmar and Thailand.\n\nNo images leave your device — all recognition runs locally.

Primary: Mon script (Myanmar Extended + Mon codepoints)
Secondary: Burmese, English, digits, punctuation

Charset: 315 characters (NFC-normalised)
Mon (mnw) is a vulnerable language. MonOCR aims to bridge the gap between physical texts and digital data.
Processing happens entirely on your device. Your data never leaves your phone.

MonOCR is built from the ground up for absolute privacy. Our edge-AI architecture ensures that 100% of optical character recognition (OCR) processing occurs entirely on your device.\n\nWe do not use loud telemetry, we do not require an account, and we do not transmit your photos or documents to any external server.

Any images you select from your library or capture via your camera are loaded straight into the Neural Processing Unit (NPU) on your local hardware. The original image and the generated text extraction both remain isolated in your device\'s memory.

If you choose to use the \"Feedback\" or \"Contribute\" features within our mobile applications, that data is saved locally to an offline database. It is not transmitted anywhere unless you manually choose to export and share those logs or screenshots with our engineering team via your own sharing apps.

To maintain our strict privacy compliance, we do not use third-party cloud crash reporters. Diagnostic logs are written to your local file system on a rolling basis. You are in full control of these logs and can export them voluntarily if you encounter bugs.

Because we do not collect data, we do not anticipate needing to update this policy often. If fundamental changes to the application architecture occur, we will reflect those in our open source repositories and in-app documentation.
If you have any questions about this privacy statement, please contact the MonDevHub engineering team via our public open source repositories on GitHub.
